title: stored six-leaf birthday search on secp256k1: 127.097776303128

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored six-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins. Each (X_k, Y_l) pair yields six x-coordinates from one batched inversion via the cube-root automorphism; the six leaves are inserted into a 2^128-slot direct-addressed table, and the first equal x-coordinate is resolved by the two linear equations m2-m1+(q2-q1)x=0 and m2+m1+(q2+q1)x=0 modulo r, then verified by [x]P=Q. The exact total is T=182071952465475957451075564855562630193850 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents (M=179 per 5x52 multiplication, A=30 per modular add/sub, 4562 per record including six table inserts), so W=T/1000=2^127.097776303128 and the claim is the least multiple of 10^-15 at or above log2 W. Peak memory is 2^133 bytes for the table plus under 2^10 bytes of state and is reported, not scored. The only heuristic is the Poisson/Chen-Stein collision bound mu=C(S,2)*2/r=0.494296, disclosed in proof.md section 5; correctness and the end-game verification are exact. ledger.py reproduces every integer and brackets 2^claim with 90-digit arithmetic; experiment.py re-checks the six-leaf formulas and full toy recoveries on y^2=x^3+7 over F_127.

experiments.purpose: Verify, on the small curve y^2=x^3+7 over F_127 (prime order 127), that phi(x,y)=(beta x,y) acts as multiplication by lambda, that the one-inversion six-leaf x formulas agree with direct affine addition, and that the birthday table plus the two linear resolution equations recover x and pass [x]P=Q. Toy scale only; it establishes neither production success nor production cost.
